title: Callvale before: PostgreSQL on one instance
claim: PostgreSQL runs on one database instance in one zone, and a failure stops the application until Ben restores a snapshot.
alt: Before: the web instance, the worker and the database instance with its data volume run in AZ 1, the database in a private subnet. Daily snapshots go to Amazon S3, and AZ 2 is empty.

edges.say: The web instance and the worker use PostgreSQL on one instance.

edges.label: patches
edges.say: Ben patches the operating system and PostgreSQL by hand.

edges.label: daily snapshot
edges.say: A daily snapshot of the data volume goes to Amazon S3.

edges.label: restore by hand
edges.say: A failure stops the application until Ben restores a snapshot.

notes: Brief 26 story pair, before (2-deep.md#decision-record, after Context). Title, claim, alt, steps from brief.json. Same cells as rds-after: web A1, worker A2, database A3, Ben A5, Amazon S3 B5 (row 4 is empty so the snapshot label sits outside the VPC); AZ 1 is column A and AZ 2 is column B (one column per Availability Zone), so the standby of rds-after lands in B3. Steps are story, not AWS rules: no fact link, no number, no absolute word. The data volume is a label on the database node, not a new node. Two columns only (three do not fit a phone).
